header.running_head: The Fervour that the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ had for Dhikr

blocks.text: thoroughbred horses (for Jihaad) from morning to night, I prefer engaging in the Dhikr of Allaah from morning to night." [^1]
Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says, "It was difficult for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) to say anything that was not the Dhikr of Allaah." [^2]
blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Abdullaah bin Mas'ood

blocks.text: Another narration states that it would upset Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) to hear anyone talking between dawn and the Fajr salaah. Yet another narration states that it was after the Fajr salaah that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) approached a group of people who were busy talking (in the Masjid). He forbade them from talking saying, "You have come here to perform salaah. You may therefore either perform your salaah or remain silent." [^3]
The Fervour Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) and Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) had for Dhikr
Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "I love more to recite 'Allaahu Akbar' a hundred times than spending a hundred gold coins in Sadaqah." [^4]

Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) said, "Rather than providing thoroughbred horses (for Jihaad) in the path of Allaah from morning to night, I prefer engaging in the Dhikr of Allaah from morning to night." [^5]
The Fervour Hadhrat Anas (RA), Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) had for Dhikr

Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) reports that they were on a journey with Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) when he heard people talking and having eloquent discussions. "O Anas," he said, "what benefit is there for me in that. Come, let us engage in the Dhikr of our Rabb because it seems like those people can even skin a person with their tongues." The rest of the narration has passed in the chapter discussing Imaan in the Aakhirah. [^6]

Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Abdullaah bin Raafi reports that he was once present in a gathering with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Umayrah (RA). Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Umayrah (RA) related to them that he had heard Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) say that he heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "There are two phrases, one of which rises no less than the height of Allaah's throne, while the other fills the atmosphere between the heavens and the earth. They are 'Laa Ilaaha Illallaah' and 'Allaahu Akbar'."
